- Can Redwood accept a 45-day notice window (instead of 60) for pilot accounts?
- Can you provide an exception path for termination-for-convenience fees during the pilot period?

I've attached CloudEdge_Redlines_v1.docx. Procurement is on copy — they'll need the definitive Order Form for signature.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Term and Renewal Clarification — CloudEdge Pilot Order

Looping in legal and contracts for review. Key asks from CloudEdge:

1) Reduce notice window to 45 days for pilot (they argue shorter timeline for pilots)
2) Waive/modify termination-for-convenience fees during pilot

Marissa — can you advise whether we can accept a 45-day notice for a time-limited pilot and what the trade-offs are? If we need a fallback, propose language we can offer (e.g., 45 days for pilot only, revert to 60 for renewals).

Kimberly — if legal signs off, can contracts generate a clean Order Form and DocuSign envelope? They want a path to signature this week.

Thanks — I'm proposing a short sync if needed.

Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Term and Renewal Clarification — CloudEdge Pilot Order

Sergio,

Thanks for the context. Quick guidance:

- 45-day notice for pilot: acceptable if we limit it contractually to the pilot term (explicit clause: "For the pilot term only, Customer notice for non-renewal shall be 45 days; thereafter, standard 60-day notice applies"). This preserves precedent.

- Termination-for-convenience (TFC) fees: we can waive any early termination fee for customers on a <=90-day pilot conditional on a minimal usage threshold and a defined offboarding SLA. Suggest language: "If Customer terminates during the pilot without cause and usage <X, fees waived; otherwise standard TFC applies." Avoid open-ended carveouts.

I've attached an annotated MSA snippet with tracked suggestions: MSA_Term_annotated_v2.docx. Kimberly — if you can incorporate Marissa's fallback language into a redlined Order Form, I think we can offer this.

-M

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_Term_annotated_v2.docx (docx)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marta Diaz <marta.diaz@cloudedge.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudedge.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term and Renewal Clarification — CloudEdge Pilot Order

Marta — thanks for the redlines. We ran your requests by legal and contracts and can offer the following compromise to keep signature timelines short:

Option A (Pilot-only compromise, recommended)
- Notice window: 45 days, explicitly limited to the pilot term
- TFC: waive early termination fee during pilot if usage < 10k inference units and Customer provides 14-day notice; otherwise standard TFC applies

Option B (Standard)
- Keep standard 60-day notice and standard TFC language

If Option A is acceptable we'll produce a clean Order Form (incorporating Marissa's precise language) and route for DocuSign. I've attached the proposed combined note for your review.

Can we set a 20-minute slot tomorrow to finalize? I can do 9:30–11:00 PT.

Best,

Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Combined_Term_Summary.txt (txt)

Sergio,

Thanks — Option A looks workable. Two quick clarifications/procurement asks:

- Can the usage threshold be defined as "billable inference units" and documented in the Order Form? Yes — procurement needs measurable metric.
- Can you confirm the waiver applies only during the official pilot period (we define pilot as the first 60 days after activation)?

Attached is our standard procurement cover sheet; procurement team asks that the final Order Form be sent as a clean PDF for signature.

If you can confirm the two bullets I'll get procurement to unblock.

Marta Diaz
